title: Best Time to Buy And Sell Stock With Cooldown
statement: You get the price of a stock on each day. You may buy and sell as often as you like, but you can hold only one share at a time, and the day after a sale you may not buy. Return the largest total profit.

example.caption: Buy at 1, sell at 2, rest, buy at 0, sell at 2. Profit 1 + 2 = 3.

output.label: best profit at the end of each day, per state

idea.sentence: Each day you are in one of three states: holding a share, just sold, or resting with nothing. Keep the best profit for each state, and say which yesterday-state each one can come from.

jargon.plain: A small set of situations you can be in, plus rules for which situation can follow which.
The day right after a sale. You must do nothing that day, so you cannot buy.

compare.unit: plans or steps (rough; plans grow exponentially, drawn as 2n)

rows.name: Brute force
rows.note: Each day: buy, sell or wait. Recurse over every choice.

rows.name: Three arrays (shown)
rows.note: One table cell per state per day. Easy to read and to trace.

rows.name: Three variables
rows.note: Each day reads only yesterday. Keep three numbers. Compute the new hold, sold and rest from the old ones, using a temporary copy.

fast.takeaway: Cooldown is not extra bookkeeping. It is a rule about which state can follow which: from sold you can only go to rest, never straight to hold.

stages.title: Day 0
stages.note: Three state arrays. On day 0 holding means buying: hold is minus the price. Sold and rest are 0.

stages.title: Hold
stages.note: Keep holding, or buy today. Buying needs yesterday to be a rest day, not a sale.

stages.title: Sold
stages.note: Sell the share held yesterday, at today's price.

stages.title: Rest
stages.note: Do nothing. Either I was already resting, or yesterday's sale cooldown just ended.

stages.title: Best ending
stages.note: End the last day owning nothing: either I sold that day, or I was resting.

edges.title: One day
edges.why: You can buy but never sell. Best profit is 0, so the loop never runs and sold and rest stay 0.

edges.title: Prices only fall
edges.why: Any trade loses money. Rest on every day.

edges.title: Steady rise
edges.why: Buying at 1 and selling at 5 beats selling every day, because each sale forces a cooldown.

edges.title: Cooldown changes the answer
edges.why: Without the cooldown rule you could sell at 3 and buy at 0 the next day, for 4. The rule costs 1.

gotchas.text: Buy from the rest state, not from the sold state. Reading sold[i-1] when buying removes the cooldown and gives answers that are too high.
Return max(sold, rest) on the last day, not hold. Ending with a share you never sold is worth nothing.
Do not start hold at 0. Owning a share has already cost money, so hold begins at -prices[0]. Starting at 0 means free shares.
With three rolling variables you must read yesterday's values before overwriting them. Assigning hold, sold and rest in sequence uses a new hold where an old one is needed. Copy to temporaries first.

recap.key: Track hold, sold and rest. hold = max(hold, rest - price). sold = hold + price. rest = max(rest, sold).
recap.complexity: Time O(n). Space O(n), or O(1) with three variables.
moves: Make three rows: hold, sold, rest
Each day: fill hold, sold, rest from yesterday
Answer is max(sold, rest) on the last day
